name: Consistency line-up
kind: Our three things beside vanilla neighbours
status: A test of three ways to make the generated models look like they belong in Skyrim, keeping Tripo H3.1's own textures. Approval is by eye here; one spot check in the game per family after.
summary: Each scene stands one of our things beside a held vanilla neighbour of the same kind (a rowboat, a Redoran hut, a Forsworn staff) under one light, with the 1.8 m person. Step through the scenes, or compare a thing as generated with the same thing graded, under one camera.

need.why: The owner ruled that our shared material looks worse than the generator's texture, and asked for another way to make a set of models consistent, approved off the game with confidence it holds in it.
need.lore: Not a lore question: a look question.
need.use: Decides how every generated model is finished before it goes to the game.

brief.text: Measure what consistent with Skyrim is, per material; grade the generated textures toward it; try a retexture from a Black Marsh building; try siblings from one approved anchor; show them all beside real neighbours.

fees.note: Fal list prices for the options used, read on 24 November 2026; not a bill.
lines: 2 sibling heads, Tripo H3.1 detailed texture

versions.label: Canoe, as generated
versions.line: Tripo H3.1's own texture beside the vanilla rowboat.
versions.made_by: Tripo H3.1; the rowboat from the game
versions.why: Already close to the game's weathered wood (distance 1.6), but its normal map is flat.

versions.label: Canoe, graded
versions.line: The same canoe, its texture graded toward the game's weathered wood.
versions.why: Distance 0.6; the wear and grain stay, the light ends come down.

versions.label: Hut, as generated
versions.line: Tripo H3.1's own texture beside the vanilla Redoran hut.
versions.made_by: Tripo H3.1; the hut from the game
versions.why: Brighter and greener than the game (distance 8.0).

versions.label: Hut, graded
versions.line: The same hut, its roots graded toward weathered wood and its leaf roof toward reed and thatch; the amber windows left alone.
versions.why: Distance 3.2: darker, less green, with the same detail. Recommended.

versions.label: Hut, densified
versions.line: The Redoran hut, the hut as generated and the hut densified, side by side. Densified: new texture layout at 420 pixels per metre (the low end of the game's weathered wood) in two 8192-pixel atlases, the generator's own texture copied onto it, and a fine grain from our hewn-cypress swatch laid along each part's own strokes.
versions.why: Same look, colour and painted features (mean lightness 28.3 before and after, chroma 12.8 before and after); close up the door and roots gain fine grain. In the game file it is 420 px per metre against 183 as generated. This web copy is cut to 2048-pixel textures so it loads on a phone: here the densified hut shows 105 px per metre and the generated one 91, so judge the grain on the close-up pictures in stage 3, not in the 3D view.

versions.label: Hut, retextured
versions.line: The hut's shell repainted by Meshy 7's retexture with a Black Marsh mud hut from the mods we hold as the style image.
versions.why: The geometry is unchanged (the same 13,248 vertices, scaled back from Meshy's 2-unit box), but it made new UVs and painted flat clay: the door, windows, roots and leaves are gone (distance 11.7).

versions.label: Glaive, as generated
versions.line: The finished glaive beside the vanilla Forsworn staff.
versions.made_by: Tripo H3.1 head, finished by hand; the staff from the game
versions.why: The obsidian is near black, darker than the game's stone (distance 6.2).

versions.label: Glaive, graded
versions.line: The same glaive, its head graded toward the game's stone, its socket toward wood and its binding toward rope.
versions.why: Distance 1.7; the obsidian reads as a dark grey stone. Your eye decides whether obsidian should stay blacker.

versions.label: Glaive family from one anchor
versions.line: The approved glaive head, and a spear head and an axe head generated from reference images drawn from its own, beside the Forsworn staff.
versions.made_by: Nano Banana 2.1 edit, then Tripo H3.1, on Fal
versions.why: Plainly one family: the same obsidian, socket and binding (distances 6.2, 4.3, 4.1). Consistent with itself, not yet with Skyrim: grade after.

stages.name: 1. What Skyrim measures as
stages.did: reference.py read meshes from the game's own archives and the mods we hold, found each material by its diffuse texture's path, and measured every shape on its real triangles and UVs: texel density, the diffuse's lightness, chroma and hue, the normal map's tilt and the specular mask.

measured.rope_and_binding: L 21.4/31.9/44.0 (10th, median, 90th), chroma 12.1, hue 78, normal tilt 22.0 deg, specular 0.1, 881.1 px per m (median of 6)
measured.bone: L 6.7/15.2/42.3 (10th, median, 90th), chroma 5.4, hue 70, normal tilt 13.4 deg, specular 0.1, 929.3 px per m (median of 24)
measured.reed_and_thatch: L 18.4/35.2/50.8 (10th, median, 90th), chroma 10.2, hue 85, normal tilt 8.2 deg, specular 0.1, 587.6 px per m (median of 10)
measured.weathered_wood: L 18.2/29.0/39.2 (10th, median, 90th), chroma 5.3, hue 85, normal tilt 7.5 deg, specular 0.1, 649.3 px per m (median of 24)
measured.stone: L 14.0/24.0/34.0 (10th, median, 90th), chroma 4.8, hue 113, normal tilt 7.4 deg, specular 0.2, 330.2 px per m (median of 24)
measured.iron_and_bronze: L 15.5/23.8/30.9 (10th, median, 90th), chroma 2.6, hue 91, normal tilt 6.5 deg, specular 0.2, 647.0 px per m (median of 24)

stages.looked: Skyrim's diffuse textures are dark and muted (median lightness 24 to 35 of 100, chroma 3 to 12), with normal maps that tilt 7 to 22 degrees; texel density is 330 px per metre for stone and 650 for wood.
stages.decision: These are the reference numbers every generated texture is measured against.

stages.name: 2. Each model against the reference
stages.did: The same measures on our models, before and after each method.

measured.Canoe, generated: L 14.8/28.6/45.7, chroma 6.5, normal 0.3 deg, 814.1 px per m; distance to weathered wood: 1.6
measured.Canoe, graded: L 19.7/28.8/37.4, chroma 5.7, normal 7.7 deg, 814.1 px per m; distance to weathered wood: 0.6
measured.Hut, generated: L 8.1/29.9/51.0, chroma 12.4, normal 0.3 deg, 182.7 px per m; distance to weathered wood: 8.0
measured.Hut, graded: L 17.1/29.0/43.8, chroma 8.5, normal 6.7 deg, 182.7 px per m; distance to weathered wood: 3.2
measured.Hut, retextured from a Black Marsh hut: L 31.3/32.7/43.7, chroma 13.3, normal none deg, 407.2 px per m; distance to weathered wood: 11.7
measured.Glaive head, generated: L 6.7/19.6/42.0, chroma 3.0, normal 1.0 deg, 6854.6 px per m; distance to stone: 6.2
measured.Glaive head, graded: L 14.2/25.5/34.7, chroma 4.6, normal 8.7 deg, 6854.6 px per m; distance to stone: 1.7
measured.Spear head, anchored sibling: L 7.7/21.1/45.0, chroma 3.4, normal 1.1 deg, 5724.5 px per m; distance to stone: 4.3
measured.Axe head, anchored sibling: L 9.3/22.3/44.8, chroma 2.4, normal 1.0 deg, 3882.5 px per m; distance to stone: 4.1

stages.looked: Grading brings all three into the game's band. The hut's texture is still softer than the game's wood (183 px per metre against 420 to 830): one texture over a whole building; that needs new UVs or a tiling detail, not a grade. The glaive head's density is far above the game's because a head is small for its texture.
stages.decision: Recommend grading (method 1), with an anchor for each family (method 3) where a set must match itself first. The retexture is rejected.

stages.name: 3. The hut's texture density
stages.did: densify.py gave the hut a new texture layout at 420 pixels per metre, copied the generator's own texture onto it texel by texel, and laid a fine grain from our hewn-cypress swatch at its true size only where the copy lacks fine detail and the colour is wood-like (not on the amber windows or the moss), turned per part to follow the painted strokes, with its own offset and scale per part. The grain only changes lightness up and down, so the colour stays. Close-ups at 1.5 m and 0.6 m beside the Redoran hut at the same distance.

measured.Hut, as generated: 183 px per m: 278.7 square metres of surface on one 4096 texture; 14,000 triangles
measured.Hut, densified: 421 px per m: two 8192 atlases (70% and 5% used), 14,000 triangles (unchanged), 1,539 charts, 5,930 vertices added along the new seams
measured.Colour: mean lightness 28.32 to 28.32, mean chroma 12.83 to 12.83 (the large atlas)
measured.Fine detail: 1.57 to 1.91 (lightness difference from a 2-pixel blur, mean over the large atlas)
measured.This page's 3D copy: textures cut to 2048: 105 px per m densified, 91 as generated
